lines.t: The vanes are spinning for you. Tamsin rarely lets them do that. Mostly she argues with them.
Welcome to Vane Hall! Those pale walls are gale curtains — wind held tight by the hall's vanes.
Out-argue a hall Tuner and their vane swings round. Down drops the curtain. Two Tuners, two curtains.
Tamsin's kin ride the wind. Electric, stone and frost voices hold their ground best in here.
This vane's mine. Blow me over and it swings your way.
Curtain's down. Feel that draught? That's the hall approving. Grudgingly.
Last curtain before the Cantor. The wind's on my side. Usually. It's fickle.
Tamsin's on her kite-deck. If she starts arguing with you, that means she likes you.
In Galewick we don't fight the wind. We argue with it, politely, until it agrees.
Ha! You argued and won. The wind respects that.
Keynote for shade. Where there's wind, there's a shadow running from it.
And an Etude — Razor Draft. Wind with an edge. Point it at problems, not people.
That foreman's work order? I read the signature. 'O. Graven, Magister.' Odile Graven.
Ysolde went pale when I said the name. There's a letter waiting for you at the Hearthrest. From Larkhollow.
Highscar Rise is west of town. Updrafts all the way up — they only lift for a gale voice singing Gust.
The ear-muff crew went that way too. Follow the wind, find the shadow.

Ha! You argued and won. The wind respects that.
Blown clean off your feet. Tie yourself down and come back.
